It is a candidate shrine (ronsha) for Uwato Shrine of Anpachi District, Mino Province, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}. (Another candidate shrine is {{ill|Ubanato Shrine (Anpachi Town)|ja|宇波刀神社 (安八町)|qid=Q11449527|lt=Uwato Shrine}} “Ubatō-jinja” in {{ill|Anpachi, Gifu|arz|انباتشى|ceb|Anpachi-chō|de|Ampachi (Gifu)|es|Anpachi (Gifu)|fa|آنپاچی، گیفو|fr|Anpachi|it|Anpachi|ja|安八町|ko|안파치정|ms|Anpachi, Gifu|my|အန်ပချိမြို့၊ ဂိဖု|pl|Anpachi|ru|Ампати (посёлок)|sv|Anpachi|tl|Anpachi, Gifu|tr|Anpachi|uk|Ампаті (Ґіфу)|ur|انپاچی، گیفو|uz|Anpachi (Gifu)|vi|Anpachi, Gifu|zh|安八町|qid=Q474384}}, Anpachi District.) Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}}, it was classified as a gōsha.

=== History and overview ===
*The date of establishment is unknown. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was known as Omon Daimyōjin and Okado Daimyōjin.
*Amid the turmoil of the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}} in the early {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, the shrine fell into ruin; the shrine buildings also deteriorated around this time, and today only a simple main sanctuary and worship hall remain.
*It is said that the shrine is currently managed by {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine (Gōdo)|ja|日吉神社 (神戸町)|qid=Q11505069|lt=Hiyoshi Shrine}}. According to one theory, in order to protect the sacred object during the chaos of the early Meiji period, the sacred object of Uwato Shrine was transferred to Hiyoshi Shrine.

=== Transportation ===
*About a 15-minute walk from {{ill|Yoro Railway|de|Yōrō Tetsudō|fr|Yoro Railway|it|Ferrovia Yōrō|ja|養老鉄道|zh|養老鐵道|qid=Q11666892}} {{ill|Hiro-Gōdo Station|id|Stasiun Hiro-Gōdo|ja|広神戸駅|jv|Setatsiyun Hiro-Gōdo|ko|히로고도역|my|ဟိရို − ဂိုးဒိုဘူတာ|ur|ہیرو-گوڈو اسٹیشن|zh|廣神戶站|qid=Q5769897}}.
